My research spans methodological statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology, and health data science. I am particularly interested in developing and evaluating statistical methods and applying them to complex biomedical and public health data.

::: {.research-section}

## Methodological Research

My methodological research focuses on **regression modeling, statistical inference, multicollinearity, shrinkage estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation**.

Current and previous work includes:

- Development and evaluation of one- and two-parameter regression estimators under multicollinearity
- Empirical comparison of Type I error and statistical power
- Ridge regression and Liu-type estimators
- Elastic Net and robust estimation methods
- Monte Carlo simulation studies
- Applications of statistical methodology to real-world datasets

:::

::: {.research-section}

## Biomedical & Public Health Research

I collaborate on interdisciplinary research involving:

- Maternal and neonatal health
- Oncology and fertility preservation
- HIV/AIDS and COVID-19
- Alzheimer's disease
- Environmental and climate health
- Population health

:::

::: {.research-section}

## Survival Analysis & Machine Learning

My work with longitudinal Alzheimer's disease data includes prediction of progression from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia.

Methods include:

- Cox proportional hazards models
- Multi-state survival analysis
- LASSO regression
- DeepSurv neural networks
- Longitudinal risk prediction
- Biomarker evaluation

:::

::: {.research-section}

## Environmental & Epidemiologic Methods

My collaborative research has involved statistical analysis of environmental exposures and health outcomes using methods including:

- Logistic regression
- Weighted Quantile Sum (WQS) regression
- Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression (BKMR)
- Structural Equation Modeling (SEM)
- Multiple imputation
- Sensitivity analysis

:::


::: {.research-goal}

### Research Goal

My broader research goal is to develop statistically rigorous and computationally useful methods that can improve analysis and decision-making in biomedical, clinical, and public health research.

:::
